Spring 2026


Beaver Conflict & Restoration Screening Tool

ArcGIS Pro Python Risk Screening Hydrology

Screens stream segments for human-beaver conflict risk and restoration opportunity, then summarizes results by county, watershed, or custom planning area. A Python tool for ArcGIS Pro that combines BRAT modeled dam capacity with NLCD land cover and impervious surface, uses ESRI Living Atlas services as default inputs, and flags low-confidence land cover for field verification.

GitHub





Fall 2025


CSU Micromobility Impact Report

Transportation Demand Management Micromobility Program Evaluation Policy

Documents the performance of CSU’s student fee-funded micromobility program in its first year, with ridership data, program outcomes, and policy recommendations for campus active transportation infrastructure. Written on behalf of ATFAB and CSU Transportation for the Association for Commuter Transportation’s 2025 Transportation Demand Management Impact Report.

Full Report (PDF) CSU Feature (p. 22)





Capstone · Spring 2026


NASA GLOBE Mosquito Habitat Mapper — CitSci Migration

Community Science Data Management Project Management Urban Ecology

Explored whether the CitSci platform could back up and expand community mosquito habitat reporting in Fort Collins by piloting a migration of NASA GLOBE Observer’s Mosquito Habitat Mapper. The final report covers project outcomes, platform assessment, stakeholder engagement, and ongoing implementation challenges.

Seeing Cities Clearly

Feature Article Remote Sensing Disaster Resilience GIS

A feature article exploring how AI-powered drone remote sensing and machine learning are transforming urban planning and disaster resilience. Examines real-world applications in land-use classification, urban forest management, historic preservation, and disaster risk mapping.

Spring 2025


Life Cycle Assessment — Soap Refill Packaging

Life Cycle Assessment OpenLCA Uncertainty Analysis Sustainability Science

Tested the common marketing claim that laminate refill pouches are better for the environment than plastic bottles, and found pouches carry equal or greater impact across most categories. Comparative LCI and LCIA in OpenLCA using ecoinvent 3.11 and ReCiPe 2016 midpoint, with Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis.

LCI Report (PDF) LCIA Report (PDF)





Spring 2025


Starship Delivery Robots — Campus Perception Study

Public Engagement Survey Research Transportation Mixed Methods

A mixed-methods study assessing student perceptions of Starship food delivery robots at CSU using in-person interviews, Likert-scale surveys, and thematic analysis. Findings revealed predominantly negative sentiment centered on inefficiency, resource misprioritization, and concerns that the robots displace more sustainable alternatives like walking and cycling.

title: Zachary Cramton
text:
Zachary Cramton
Spatial Data for Resilient, Livable Communities

LinkedIn GitHub Email


Fourmile Creek, Fairplay, CO ©2026 Zachary Cramton





The greatest potential to improve daily life is in the places people live and build, where environmental damage is concentrated and the most people feel its effects. Restoring remote forests and habitat is important for the broader environment, but it doesn’t always have the visible, direct impact needed to build support and funding for future projects.
I studied Ecosystem Science and Sustainability at Colorado State University, specializing in climate resilience and public education. My work includes transportation planning, environmental analysis, and GIS projects. I have directed $1.5 million in matching funds to successful grant applications totaling over $7 million for multimodal transportation infrastructure.
Recent work includes a spatial screening tool for beaver conflict and restoration analysis, built with Python in ArcGIS Pro, and a micromobility impact report (pg. 22) for the Association for Commuter Transportation. As project manager for my senior capstone, I piloted the migration of NASA GLOBE Observer’s Mosquito Habitat Mapper to the CitSci platform in Fort Collins.
